I generally agree with most complaints about PC language. It IS coddling, there's no doubt in my mind about that. There's also a lot of impracticality in it. For instance, you have to tread on eggshells these days because it's almost impossible to keep up with whatever new thing the PC brigade has decided to be offended over. If I need to talk to someone, I want to be able to just start talking to them, I don't want to have to preface every interaction with a carefully constructed verbal chess game designed to delicately divine the precise gender identity and sexuality of the person I want/need to talk to. These people manage to find a way to make EVERYONE an insensitive oaf, because they've built a narrative that ensures their perpetual victimhood. Pandering to these people is just madness. So obviously I am very much on the side of anti-PC. (and by the way, I'm politically liberal, so lets dispense with that stereotype)

However.

Many of the most vocal groups complaining about political correctness are in fact people who have very controversial views. When people who say controversial things eventually face public disapproval, they sometimes accuse the public of being "PC". This is just racists, bigots and assholes who want special privileges (ie, want to be coddled) to say whatever they want without consequences. They are no different than the standard PC brigade who don't want to face reality and accept the fact that their opinions are just unpopular.

So on the one hand you have SJW extremists who want everything to be coddled and censored and want gender and sexuality to be the most important topic discussed ever. On the other hand you have neo-nazi extremists who can't figure the difference between "disapproval" and "censorship". In the middle you've got moderate, regular folk who just shrug their shoulders and say "it doesn't affect me so I guess it's all okay".

PC is the enemy of a free republic, and I don't mean that lightly. If you start policing speech on topics even a majority of people may agree is taboo it becomes problematic. Why? Because it can be turned into law. Suddenly there is a mechanism to punish individuals if they do not speak according to a set of ethics determined by someone else. It wouldn't take long before corupt leaders found ways to manipulate that mechanism to suppress opposition to maintain power. Think this is far fetched? We are seeing a manipulation of rules and policies Playing out right now in the primaries on both sides of the aisle. If anyone honestly believes censorship would not be abused in the same manner, they are nieve.

What I'm trying to get at is that no one can truly be PC all the time because there are no mind readers. Even if one tries to espouse (or not) their version of PC-ness as they see it there will always be someone out there who might accuse you of spouting misogynistic or racist or anti semitic rhetoric.
